title: upstream finding: init --update reads accidental payload loss as deliberate deletion
description: Observed during the 2026-07-20 install repair: crosslink init --update classifies absent managed files as 'deleted by user, skipping (will not recreate)' — a git clean or re-clone is indistinguishable from deliberate deletion, so accidental loss becomes sticky policy: the safe repair path preserves the hollow shell and only --force restores it. Suggestion: distinguish recorded deletion (a manifest tombstone written by an actual removal act) from mere absence; absence with no tombstone should offer restoration or at least report loudly. Joins the upstream findings list. Evidence: this repo's dry-run output, 2026-07-20; the hollow-shell audit on the amendment issue.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: Migrated to the canonical upstream (operator-directed workflow, decision on #597): re-verified STILL-LIVE at dollspace-gay/crosslink main 85691369 — manifest.rs:141 maps absence straight to UpdateAction::Deleted, no tombstone field exists; second --update recreates via manifest drop (mod.rs:795-797) — and filed as dollspace-gay/crosslink#13, which supersedes this record. Evidence: the evaluation scout reports and draft bodies on #597's trail, 2026-07-20.
